title: Mariana Grajales Women's Platoon
summary: In September 1958 Fidel Castro and the Rebel Army general staff formed an all-women combat platoon in Cuba's Sierra Maestra, named for Mariana Grajales, mother of the Maceo brothers. Thirteen women, under Isabel Rielo, served in the final months of the revolutionary war.

uncertainty.note: Sources give 4 September 1958; Fidel Castro's own account, quoted in Juventud Rebelde, places the organising meeting on 3 September, ending at 1 a.m. on the 4th.

importance.justification: First organised women's combat unit of Cuba's Rebel Army, symbolic in later accounts of women in the revolution.

reviewer_note: All sources are Cuban state or state-aligned outlets, so the framing is one-sided; no independent scholarly source was opened. Date is 3 or 4 September 1958. Pin is the Sierra Maestra range centre, not the La Plata command post (no opened coordinate), hence 60 km uncertainty. Platoon size (13) and leader (Isabel Rielo) come from Juventud Rebelde and Prensa Latina.
